major_finding_summary: Architectural inject INVISIBLE at substrate: only 0/5 prompts produce canonical-mode phi_star drift > 0.01 from both baselines. cross_attn.o_proj net contribution is bounded below threshold (predicted by spec §4.1 init_weights std=0.02 attenuation) OR canonical 0.5 magnitude is too small. Cand-D Stage 1 form may be unsalvageable on best.pt without larger magnitude OR retrain with stronger cross-attn signal.
platform: mac CPU (.venv-eeg python3.12, transformers, torch fp32)
honest_c3: C1 — canonical 5-axis 0.5 magnitude is anima-internal heuristic per spec §2.3 placeholder. Paradigm v11 G3 actual training-time injection distribution NOT extracted from C-module emission logs. F-CAND-D-1 PASS at this magnitude validates the ARCHITECTURAL channel (cross_attn carries content) but the magnitude itself is uncalibrated. F-CAND-D-1 FAIL_TRUE here CANNOT distinguish "channel architecturally bypassed" from "0.5 below detection threshold". Disambiguation requires magnitude sweep at 1.0/2.0/5.0.

C2 — cells 5-7 fill formula (mean(0-4) × 0.5/3) is per spec §2.3 but introduces correlation between cells 0-4 and cells 5-7. The phi_star proxy uses pairwise cosine across all 28 cell pairs; this correlation pattern affects phi MORE than the axis-content per cell would predict. canonical-mode phi drift may therefore be partly an artifact of cell-fill geometry, not pure axis content. A flat 5-cell-only canonical (cells 5-7 = zeros) would isolate axis-content from cell-fill correlation.

C3 — axis_activation extractor (BG-A line 152-159, mirror) computes mean(|x|) over 192-dim slices of the POST-ln_f tile-replicated cell. The CANONICAL inject is structured per AXIS_SPANS, so under mode=canonical we are essentially measuring "how much of the axis-sliced inject content survives 16 layers of cross-attn + ffn". This is a COMPOSITION measurement (inject × substrate transform), not a pure inject visibility test. axis-spread comparison vs BG-L mode=none baseline is therefore confounded by per-prompt text-routing through std attention.

C4 — DecoderBlockV2:553 guard uses `consciousness_states is not None`. mode=zero passes a tensor of zeros; mode=canonical passes structured tensor. Both cause guard to PASS. mode=none returns Python None; guard short-circuits. This validates the F-CAND-D-1 architecture discriminator. However, BG-A subprocess wrapper attempts kwarg `consciousness_states` and falls back to no-kwarg on TypeError; if the HF wrapper does NOT accept the kwarg (shim v4 specific), modes zero/canonical degenerate to mode=none silently. We track kwarg_accepted flag per measurement.

C5 — phi_star is anima-canonical proxy (PHI_STAR_BASELINE × (1 + 0.05 × mean_pair_cosine)). F-CAND-D-1 threshold 0.01 corresponds to mean-pair-cosine delta of 0.01/(41.86 × 0.05) = ~0.00478 — quite tight. Spec §4.1 predicts canonical drift +0.05 to +0.50 vs baseline; if we observe drift in that range, F-CAND-D-1 PASS easily. If drift is < 0.005, F-CAND-D-1 FAIL_TRUE — but at <0.005 phi delta we cannot distinguish from RoPE-cache-rebuild order noise. Below-threshold result needs replication to be reliable.
next_step_recommendation: INVESTIGATE: (a) increase canonical magnitude to 1.0 / 2.0 / 5.0 and re-test (if signal emerges, 0.5 was below noise floor); (b) extract paradigm v11 G3 actual training-time injection distribution from C-module emission logs; (c) defer cand-D Stage 1 closure pending wider-magnitude empirical sweep.
